sections.content:
You know *a pesar de*, *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32, and *aun cuando* from B2 Unit 8. At C1, choosing among these forms and the concessive future from Lesson 1 depends on register, clause structure and whether the obstacle is a settled fact or an open possibility.

In lively speech, the **concessive future** (*Será un desembolso enorme, pero...*) grants an opponent's argument quickly before pivoting. In neutral or written prose, **pese a** and **a pesar de** condense an obstacle into a noun phrase or infinitive (*pese al sobrecosto*, *a pesar de exigir un sacrificio*). Before a full clause, *a pesar de que* takes the indicative for a known fact and the subjunctive for an unconfirmed or hypothetical obstacle.

In columns, speeches and formal argument, **aun cuando** (written without an accent on *aun*) raises the emphasis: it takes the indicative for a real fact (*aun cuando el presupuesto era limitado*) and the subjunctive for a possible or future obstacle (*aun cuando el proyecto no resulte rentable al principio*). Pair any of these with *así y todo* in a second sentence to restate that the conclusion still holds.

sections.title: Choosing the right concessive frame
rows: *Será un desembolso grande, pero el servicio mejora.*
*pese a* / *a pesar de* + noun or infinitive (neutral / formal)
*Pese al sobrecosto, el proyecto sigue adelante.*
*a pesar de que* + indicative (fact) or subjunctive (hypothetical)
*A pesar de que hubo críticas, la medida fue rentable.*
*Aun cuando exija un sacrificio, defenderemos el plan.*

items.spanish: Pese al sobrecosto inicial, el servicio resultó rentable al segundo año.
items.english: Despite the initial cost overrun, the service turned out to be cost-effective in the second year.

items.spanish: A pesar de que muchos hablaron de despilfarro, los datos muestran lo contrario.
items.english: Although many spoke of a waste of money, the data show the opposite.

items.spanish: Aun cuando parezca un capricho caro, el proyecto responde a una necesidad real.
items.english: Even if it seems an expensive whim, the project answers a real need.

items.spanish: El desembolso exige un sacrificio; así y todo, conviene aprobarlo.
items.english: The outlay requires a sacrifice; even so, it is advisable to approve it.

sections.content: Never drop *que* before a conjugated verb (*pese a hubo problemas* ✗ → *pese a que hubo problemas* ✓ or *pese a los problemas* ✓). And keep *aun* unaccented in *aun cuando*: with an accent, *aún* means "still".
